name: Corsican paghjella modern revival
lineage: Corsican paghjella three-voice male polyphonic singing tradition of Corsica (France). Performance: three male singers in close-position polyphonic configuration: a bassu low-register foundational voice, a sicunda middle-register voice, and a terza high-register ornamental voice, all male-only, performing sacred (especially the canonical Mass-of-the-Dead repertoire) and secular repertoire. The genre nearly disappeared by the mid-twentieth century but was revived through the 1970s riacquistu Corsican-cultural-revival movement under the canonical group A Filetta. Distinguished from Sardinian cantu a tenore by Corsican paghjella's three-voice-male (vs four-voice-with-guttural-bass) configuration.
